facts.fact: The diagnostic states that the civil register stays on paper ledgers at the Sector offices, and that each time a page is written a loose NIDA notification form is filled, collected on an ongoing basis and keyed into the electronic National Population Register at a central facility in Kigali by a staff of about 30 (research early 2015; no date given, published 2016).
facts.system: Civil Register, keyed by NIDA into the National Population Register

facts.fact: The diagnostic states that a NIDA notification form is generated for every page written in any of the Sector registers, which include the birth and death volumes (also marriage, sector entry and exit), and that the forms are entered into the National Population Register (no date given; published 2016).
facts.system: Civil Register, keyed by NIDA into the National Population Register

facts.fact: The diagnostic states that the civil register 'is not computerized yet': the 416 Sector offices record declarations by hand in bound annual volumes kept in duplicate, and none enters data electronically, entry being done centrally by NIDA in Kigali (no date given; published 2016).
facts.system: Civil Register, keyed by NIDA into the National Population Register

facts.fact: The diagnostic states that a web-based pilot of online registration at health institutions was launched in 2014 by the National Institute of Statistics of Rwanda in coordination with NIDA; it gives no count of institutions.
facts.system: Web-based pilot registration at health institutions

facts.fact: The diagnostic states that the Sector Executive Secretary is the Civil Register Officer and that NIDA, an agency established by Law 43/2011 under the supervision of MINALOC, collects the register's information and maintains the National Population Register (no date given; published 2016).
facts.system: Civil Register, keyed by NIDA into the National Population Register

facts.fact: The diagnostic states that NIDA, which does the keying, has for several years covered its entire operating budget from the fees for its own services, with no allocation of government funds; this is NIDA's self-financing as a whole, not a budget line for civil registration (no date given; published 2016).
facts.system: Civil Register, keyed by NIDA into the National Population Register

facts.fact: The diagnostic states that Rwanda was reviewing a five-year reform to move civil registration to a digital platform, with a draft law under consideration, but that the authors had seen no detailed plan and the country had decided to run an APAI-CRVS assessment before committing to one (no date given; published 2016).

systems.system: Civil Register, keyed by NIDA into the National Population Register
systems.platform: Paper ledgers; purpose-built data entry software at NIDA
systems.owner: Sector Executive Secretary as Civil Register Officer; National Identification Agency (NIDA) for the keying
systems.tiers: Paper registers at 416 Sector offices; notification forms keyed centrally in Kigali

systems.system: Web-based pilot registration at health institutions
systems.owner: National Institute of Statistics of Rwanda (NISR) with NIDA

systems.tiers: Central electronic database at NIDA in Kigali; baseline door-to-door registration of 9.2 million in 2007, about 10.7 million entries in early 2015
Biometric enrolment at Sector offices sharing 163 enrolment kits among 416; about 6.5 million people enrolled; online identity verification services for relying parties
